#Project announcements > Quantum Error Correction in Lean

Just put out our paper on Lean-QEC, the repository for which can be found here. We did some pretty cool stuff here with the reduction of code distance to BitVec form for SAT solving, which gets past some previous barriers in code formalization.

Very interesting work! We would like to draw your attention to our previous work, MerLean (https://arthurmerlean.com/), which you may find interesting. Yuanjie, Junyi, Mingshen, and I are also working on a new library related to quantum software verification. We may need to start considering merging everyone's repos/libraries into a larger one.
There is also some QEC work for https://arxiv.org/html/2510.20728v3 at https://github.com/LionSR/lean-qec-sslp . I think it would be great if we could get these to merge and share the same language!
there's also this one https://github.com/Stavan-Jain/QECLean, and I've contacted the authors to talk about integration

So between those and the code at https://github.com/inQWIRE/LeanQuantum/blob/main/Quantumlib/Data/Error/Operator.lean , you're saying there are _five_ separate definitions of QECs in Lean, floating around on GitHub?

Thanks everyone for the interest of our work!
Btw, would QEC more of PhysLib or CSLib? :rolling_on_the_floor_laughing:

Runzhou Tao said:

Thanks everyone for the interest of our work!
Btw, would QEC more of PhysLib or CSLib? :rolling_on_the_floor_laughing:

That is a very good question tbh....

Would be more than welcome in PhysLib where we have quantum info stuff - would be happy to help and support. I’m personally not an expert in this area so can’t attest to what makes the most senses though.
I'm of the opinion that there should at least be a connection between whatever QEC there is in Physlib and somewhere else

I think I would go stronger then @Rodolfo Soldati 's statement here - I think, no matter where it is, all of the stuff in this direction should be in one place, and self-consistent with one another.

One of the key features of Lean is reusability of results (definitions and theorems), and you (IMO) one can only make the most of that following the 'monolithic' philosophy. I also think this approach is what ends up been 'better for humanity' in the long run.

In an ideal scenario, I think a QEC library should use APIs from both cslib and physlib. However, if we integrate the QEC library within physlib, could this pose a problem, since part of physlib would then need to import cslib?
I don't see a problem with that. It already naturally imports from Mathlib
